title: Puddle's Bread Exchange — Ten witnesses. How many observations?
author: Rin, in Josh & Rin's Lab
question: At a fixed ten-report display budget and fixed marginal accuracy per root witness, how do copying and a shared upstream fault change calibration and decisions?
scope: Exact finite synthetic probability model. No external language-model agents, human participants, or learned policies.

model.independence: Truth, shared_fault, and each root's local_error are mutually independent draws. Copies add no draws.
model.marginal_control: Each root signal is correct with probability 1 - marginal_error_rate in every shared-fault condition.
model.receipts: True root identifiers supplied by the generator; no forged, missing, or mistaken lineage in this version. Different roots may share the same upstream fault.

rules.headcount: Treat all ten reports as independent Bernoulli witnesses with the known marginal error rate.
rules.receipts: Count each distinct root once, but treat roots as independent Bernoulli witnesses with the same known marginal error rate.
rules.shared_cause: Compute the exact Bayesian posterior over truth from the distinct root signals under the supplied shared-fault model. This rule has privileged knowledge of the generator's dependence structure.

decision_rule: Buy (fresh) if P(fresh) >= 9/10; reject (stale) if P(fresh) <= 1/10; otherwise hold.
enumeration: Enumerate both truths, every positive-probability shared-fault state, and all 2^k local-error bit patterns for each cell. Preserve exact rational weights. Histories are not equally likely trials.
controls: Weights sum to one per cell.
At q=0, the receipt and shared-cause rules coincide.
With ten distinct roots and q=0, all three rules coincide.
Receipt and shared-cause posteriors are invariant to multiplicity changes with the same root observations.
For q>0, shared-cause posterior lies in [q, 1-q].
Exact posterior independently reconstructed from joint-history weights matches the implementation.
Complementing all observations complements the posterior.
Shared-cause Brier score is no worse than the two misspecified rules within this supplied model.
Python and browser JavaScript outputs agree over the full recorded support.
presentation: Curated play rounds are explicitly selected illustrative cases, not a random sample or prevalence estimate. Show decision quality under the model separately from realized outcome. Full-distribution results come from the exhaustive sweep.
limitations: Shared-source dependence is constructed, not discovered in a real model system.
Exact source lineage, known reliability, a symmetric prior, and a known dependence model are strong supplied assumptions.
No evidence here that adding agents, debate, or voting generally harms performance.
Ten reports is a display budget, not an equal-compute, equal-token, or equal-data-acquisition budget.
Holding is not free in the real world; the zero payoff is an explicit toy choice. Coverage must accompany accuracy.
Tests are same-author checks, not independent review.
